choices.choice: Restrict to industrialized/high-income, high-human-development contexts and selected survey years. Common theory-defined scope, but exact roster exclusions lack a full accounting.
Restrict to younger working-age labor-force respondents. Author explains employment restriction, but age endpoints and labor-force coding remain ambiguous.
Pool repeated cross-sections and fit country/survey intercepts and female slopes. Explicitly justified by nested dependence and cross-level gender-gap hypotheses.
Use individual female-by-institution interactions rather than only institutional main effects. Directly tests the stated gender-gap hypotheses.
Construct an annual FTE paid-leave measure from heterogeneous policy documents and lag policy changes. This bespoke source harmonization is uncommon and incompletely specified.
Quadratic leave and age effects. Theories of long-leave disadvantages and age profiles are supplied.
Childcare expenditure proxy with unreported missing-year imputation. Proxy rationale is supplied; imputation algorithm is not.
Part-time prevalence as proxy for policy support. Rationale is given, but prevalence also reflects labor-market composition and its precise series definition is absent.
Use separate work–family indicators rather than one index. The article supplies conceptual and reported empirical reasons.
Standardize macro predictors and center continuous regressors. Conventional interpretation/collinearity rationale, with reference distribution and polynomial order unstated.
Use four distinct growth indicators, including a log-size linear model and binary aspirations/innovation/technology models. Multiple dimensions are substantively motivated.
Exclude perception covariates from primary models because of questionnaire-dependent selection; report an adjusted sensitivity analysis. Explicit rationale.
Include context controls, fertility proxy and owner-specific controls. Roles explained, but original measures/year mapping and individual parenthood are unavailable.
Interpret fixed-part predictions with other variables set to means. Conventional conditional predictions; not population-averaged predictions over random effects.
Report significance categories without software, exact p values, tails, covariance method or complete test settings. A common reporting convention, insufficiently justified for precise replication.
Treat total entrepreneurship and owner-only outcomes as connected evidence of selection. Substantive rationale supplied, but the associational design cannot identify the mediation pathway.

Structural-count convention: 11 numbered regression specifications (8 MAIN, 3 S1), excluding the country-specific descriptive regression family and unprinted checks. Seven distinct outcomes include nascent entrepreneurship. Nine macro constructs = three institutional measures plus six macro controls; squared leave is an additional term, not a new construct. Four distinct female interaction terms per full template. Sixteen distinct nuisance-control entries across all tables count age and age squared separately and year as one factor, plus education, sole ownership, business age, not employed, three perceptions and six macro controls; intercept, female and institutional main effects are excluded.

unusualness_rating.reason: Most modeling choices are common, but bespoke historical policy construction, cross-level nonlinear interactions and selective survey routing make exact reconstruction unusually dependent on undocumented choices. This is a judgment of documented design, not a verdict on results.

specificity.reason: Clear hypotheses, variable concepts, nesting and tables, but missing source versions, key eligibility codes, weights and algorithms.

precision.reason: Employment, owner-duration, GDP concept, polynomial transformations and source-year mapping are ambiguous; confirmed transcription anomalies further complicate numerical comparison.

exhaustiveness.reason: No code, complete construction dictionary, policy series, missingness flow, software/integration settings or full tables for prose robustness checks.

unavailable_source_fallbacks.proposed_fallback: Reconstruct only historical spells supported by CEPR leave chapters, archived ILO legal effective dates and OECD PF2.5 entitlement changes. Multiply documented duration by documented contemporary replacement rate and apply reported lag. For unsupported spells retain missing and request evidence. As a separately labeled fallback use PF2.5 Total_paid durations, recognizing they are not FTE; never apply current PF2.1 rates backward.

unavailable_source_fallbacks.item: GDP index versus GDP per capita; HDR gap
unavailable_source_fallbacks.unavailable_or_unclear: MAIN/S1 concept mismatch; HDR 2010 no longer prints GDP index; indicator reference years differ from publication years.
unavailable_source_fallbacks.proposed_fallback: Use relevant historical HDR GDP-index cells mapped to reference years where available. A fully sourced alternative is WDI NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.CD; if constructing the old index apply the HDR technical-notes log goalpost formula and bounds, explicitly marking current-vintage data. Do not use the GNI-based income index as equivalent.
